actual_checks: Full exact report, literal prompt, provenance/source records and full earlier integer-family/discriminant-search contribution read. The complete all-prime-power/all-modulus local theorem with a proof at singular prime 3 is a distinct substantive congruence classification, explicitly classical with no novelty or global representation claim.
Cauchy–Davenport is proved over the prime field using a total-degree coefficient formula. If |A|+|B|>p direct intersection proves full sumset; otherwise the binomial coefficient at degree |A|+|B|-2

Cube-image cardinality is p or (p+2)/3; two sumset applications give every residue for p!=3. Target zero uses (1,-1,0) to retain a unit coordinate, including p=2. Ordinary Hensel digit correction uses invertible 3x^2 and preserves the unit.

At 3, precisely residues 0,+/-1,+/-2,+/-3 occur modulo 9, all with a unit-coordinate choice. For a>=2, x -> x+t3^(a-1) changes its cube by t x^2 3^a modulo 3^(a+1); the other terms have valuations 2a-1 and 3a-3, both >=a+1 even at a=2. Hence all higher lifts work and coordinate updates are Cauchy despite not keeping each earlier coordinate residue unchanged at its old index. CRT applied separately to three coordinates proves all-modulus sufficiency; m=9 gives necessity.

The p-adic/real points are local, with the triple allowed to depend on modulus. Success at every modulus does not supply one ordinary integral triple or infinitude. No integral Hasse principle or height bound is inferred.
